recipes.name: Harvest Pepper and Chicken Pasta
ingredients_raw: 2 chicken breasts, cut into thin strips
1 clove garlic, minced, or more to taste
0.5 (26 ounce) jar tomato sauce (such as Newman's Own®)

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook bow-tie pasta at a boil, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 12 minutes. Drain.

Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken strips; cook and stir until no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, 5 to 7 minutes. Transfer to a plate lined with paper towels.

Reduce heat under skillet to medium; add onion, orange bell pepper, red bell pepper, garlic, dried basil, and red pepper flakes to skillet. Cook and stir until onions are translucent and peppers are softened, 3 to 5 minutes. Add tomato sauce; heat for about 2 minutes. Add chicken; cook for another 2 to 3 minutes. Portion cooked pasta into bowls; spoon chicken and sauce mixture on top.

raw_recipe.headline: Harvest Pepper and Chicken Pasta
raw_recipe.description: This quick and easy recipe makes a budget-friendly skillet of colorful bell peppers, jarred red sauce, and chicken breast served over pasta.

review.reviewBody: This is ok but not good as is, you would have to modify it. I made it bc last minute I needed a simple pasta with chicken, but these flavors do not help the chicken any. I mean it tastes exactly as you would think it would if you look at the ingredients list, I am not sure what I was expecting. More tomatoes, more garlic, salt, and more herbs would have helped.

This is a quick and easy recipe, as described. I followed the recipe pretty closely. I added a splash of red wine at the end, which added some richness. We really enjoyed it for a weeknight dinner. I was looking for a recipe to use some of our garden bounty of peppers. Perfect!

Very easy and tasty. I think I cut back on the pepper just a bit and I am glad I did.. nice bite to it. I tried it chunky and then pureed it as well. Good both ways. I found a cute pumpkin shaped pasta so I used that
